h2: Liquid penetrant testing services: what US buyers specify
html:
Most requests for liquid penetrant testing services in the US are for field work on welds, castings and machined parts: a fabricator needs PT on stainless or nickel-alloy welds where magnetic particle testing cannot be used, or a plant needs PT on a repair before it returns to service. Buyers write the same request as dye penetrant testing, liquid penetrant inspection, PT or, for the fluorescent process, FPI.

Visible dye or fluorescent?

Visible (Type II, red dye) penetrant is the field default: it needs no darkened area and is examined in white light. Fluorescent penetrant inspection (Type I) is more sensitive and is examined under UV-A light in a darkened area, which suits shop work and fine cracking. The removal method matters as much as the type: solvent-removable for field spot checks, water-washable or post-emulsifiable for production work. The procedure has to name both, along with the dwell time and the developer.

Which code or standard applies

For pressure equipment and piping, ASME Section V Article 6 sets the method and the construction code sets acceptance, for example ASME Section VIII or B31.3. ASTM E165 is the general-industry practice, while ASTM E1417 with AMS 2644 materials governs aerospace and other critical-part work. For structural steel, AWS D1.1 applies. The report should name the standard, the penetrant system by manufacturer and batch, the surface temperature, the dwell time, and every relevant indication with its size and location.

Where PT is not the right method

Penetrant finds only flaws open to the surface. It will not find subsurface cracking, it is unreliable on rough, porous or painted surfaces, and on ferromagnetic steel it is slower than magnetic particle inspection, which also finds near-surface flaws. For volumetric weld examination use ultrasonic testing or radiography. Aerospace production lines that must hold Nadcap accreditation for penetrant processing are outside the field service described here.

Ordering PT

Atlantis NDT technicians are certified to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and every report is reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III. Tell us the material, the code and acceptance criteria, the number and type of welds or parts, and any limit on penetrant chemistry, such as low-halogen and low-sulfur materials for stainless steel and nickel alloys. See also all NDT inspection services, or train your own staff with penetrant testing training. To book work, request a quote.
